title: Taking Reinforcement Learning Cross Datacenter — Nan Jiang, Modal
talk_summary: Modal's Nan Jiang describes decoupling RL rollout workers from the tightly-coupled trainer cluster by shipping sparse, bit-exact weight deltas instead of full checkpoints, since ~99% of BF16-visible weights are unchanged per optimizer step due to Adam's small update magnitude versus BF16 rounding granularity. A version-aware proxy lets globally scattered inference engines self-sync to a published weight version and serve requests with explicit version contracts.

takeaways.technique: Versioned artifact contracts for distributed workers
takeaways.what_they_do: Trainer publishes immutable rollout weight versions to a shared bulletin board; each remote engine pulls the latest version, and a proxy checks whether an engine is at an acceptable version, applies missing transitions, or returns 'not ready'.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If the version is already at acceptable commit version, the psychar just proxy the request. If the engine is behind but can they can catch up the psychar just apply the missing transition.

takeaways.what_they_do: Requests carry both the version being sent to and the version acceptable to receive; responses echo the exact version plus metadata (tokens, logprobs, replay info) so the consumer can validate consistency.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a request does not just say give me the completion. You will also say which version you will be sending request to and which version you will be accepting

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of transferring full checkpoints (hundreds of GB), they compute a sparse bit-exact diff of only changed served weights and transfer that (hundreds of MB).
takeaways.evidence_quote: the link shrinks from hundreds of gigabytes to maybe hundreds of megabytes
takeaways.numbers: ~99% of BF16 weights bit-identical per step; ~0.05-0.15% changed in an FP8 run; 500GB -> ~500MB transfer

takeaways.technique: Elastic worker pool decoupled from a fixed coordinator
takeaways.what_they_do: Rollout (serving) workers run outside the trainer cluster across regions/providers and autoscale; only the tightly-coupled trainer stays on fast fabric.
